correctness.rationale: The forced-leaf-set deletion bijection yields (n-k)^(n-k-2) residual trees; the center's residual degree gains k and exactly k selected leaves retain degree one. Summing these conditional degree-bin differences proves the exact formula. A controlled fixed-degree binomial expansion proves the limit; the factorial comparison gives strict signs including the k=2 exception. Independently enumerated 280388 trees passed 100 exact rational identities, which corroborate but do not substitute for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected primary works address finite fringe-subtree asymptotics (Berzunza Ojeda–Holmgren–Janson), degree–degree covariance (Ekhad–Zeilberger), or proper-cherry marginals (Junk–Schmidt–Weber). Statement-level comparison did not find an implication covering the exact uniform-Cayley unrestricted-center fan–degree cross covariance and universal asymptotic sign classes. Searches also compared aliases such as leaf-neighbor sets, pendant k-stars, cherries and Prüfer degree counts. General generating-function rediscovery remains a real historical risk.

value.rationale: The pendant k-leaf fan is a motivated local symmetry statistic, while degree counts are basic structural statistics. All-orders mixed moments quantify their interaction and the explicit fixed-degree limit gives a universal, nonobvious positive–negative–positive dependence structure, with a distinct two-leaf transition. This fills an interpretable joint fluctuation gap not answered by degree-only moments or proper-cherry marginals.
